lessons.title: Knowing weeds and why we remove them
lessons.html:
Knowing weeds and why we remove them

A weed is a plant growing where we do not want it. In a mealie field, a pumpkin plant can be a weed. Most weeds grow fast and strong.

Why weeds are a problem

  • They take water, food (nutrients) and sunlight from the crop.
  • They hide insects and diseases.
  • They make harvesting slow and difficult.
  • Some weeds are poisonous to animals.
  • Weed seeds in the harvest lower its quality and price.

Common weeds in South Africa

  • Blackjacks (knapsekêrel): the seeds stick to clothes.
  • Nutgrass (uintjie): grows from small bulbs under the ground.
  • Pigweed (misbredie).
  • Thorn apple (stinkblaar): poisonous to people and animals.
  • Couch grass (kweek): spreads with runners under the ground.

Your supervisor will show you the weeds on your farm and how to tell them apart from the crop. Always make sure you know which plant is the crop before you start.

Annual and perennial weeds

Annual weeds live for one season and grow again from seed. If you remove them before they flower, they cannot make new seed. Perennial weeds live for many years. They grow back from roots, bulbs or runners, so you must remove the whole root.

When to weed

Weed early, when the weeds are small. Small weeds come out easily and have not yet taken much water from the crop. The most important time is the first weeks after the crop comes up. Weeding after rain, when the soil is soft, makes pulling easier. Hoeing works best when the soil surface is dry, so the cut weeds dry out and die.

Never let weeds make seed. One weed plant can drop thousands of seeds, which will grow for many years.

lessons.title: Weeding safely by hand and hoe
lessons.html:
Weeding safely by hand and hoe

Tools

  • Hands (wear gloves): for weeds close to the crop.
  • Hoe (skoffel): for cutting weeds between rows.
  • Spade or fork: for digging out deep roots and bulbs.
  • Slasher or sickle: for cutting tall weeds on edges and roads.

How to pull weeds

  1. Hold the weed low down, near the soil.
  2. Pull slowly and straight up so the root comes out.
  3. For weeds with deep roots, loosen the soil first with a fork.
  4. Shake off the soil and put the weed in a pile or bag.

How to hoe

  1. Keep the hoe blade sharp.
  2. Cut the weeds just under the soil surface. Do not dig deep; you can damage crop roots.
  3. Work backwards so you do not step on the cut weeds and push them back into the soil.
  4. Keep a safe distance from the crop plants.

Getting rid of weeds

Weeds with seeds, bulbs or runners must be removed from the field. Put them in bags and take them to the place your supervisor shows you. Weeds without seeds can be left in the sun between rows to dry.

Safety

  • Wear gloves, closed shoes, a hat and long sleeves.
  • Drink water often and rest in the shade on hot days.
  • Bend your knees, not your back, and change position often.
  • Carry tools with the blade pointing down and keep space between workers.
  • Watch out for snakes in long grass. Never try to catch or kill a snake; move away and tell your supervisor.
  • Wash your hands before eating. Do not touch poisonous weeds like thorn apple with bare hands.

Check your work

After weeding, look back down the row. No weeds should be left, and crop plants should not be damaged.

Key points

  • Weeds take water, nutrients and light from the crop.
  • Weed early, before weeds flower and make seed.
  • Remove the whole root of perennial weeds.
  • Hoe shallowly and keep away from crop roots.
  • Wear PPE, drink water and watch out for snakes.
